title: Nodal torus chart with canonical punctured action
statement: For a commutative ring $A$ and $\pi\in A$, use the actual nodal algebra and standard affine model of [def-trf-strict-semistable-curve], $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A[s,t]/(st-\pi))$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Use its canonical coordinate sections $s,t$ from [lem-trf-ordered-nodal-branch-overlap]. Schemes and affine spectra have the meanings of [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]; group objects have the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], over this arbitrary base. Let $G=\mathbf G_{m,A}=\operatorname{Spec}A[z,z^{-1}]$ be the multiplicative group of [def-sfb-split-torus-over-ring], with its Laurent Hopf group law $z\mapsto z\otimes z$, identity $z\mapsto1$ and inverse $z\mapsto z^{-1}$. An action of $G$ on $X$ is standard if, on every test $A$-scheme $T$, every $z_0:T\to G$ and $x:T\to X$, its two pulled-back coordinate functions are $z_0s(x)$ and $z_0^{-1}t(x)$, respectively. There is a unique such action; use it as the standard action. Put $U=D(s)\cup D(t)$ and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the actual open inclusion, with its inherited map to $\operatorname{Spec}A$. There is a unique action on $U$ for which $j(z_0x)=z_0j(x)$ on every test scheme; use this as the restricted action. All choices are determined uniquely by the displayed coordinate and inclusion equations.

source.place: Author-hosted https://sites.math.washington.edu/~jarod/papers/iwahori.pdf; Section 2, Claims 1--2, printed p.2; Section 3, Theorem 1.3 (1) implies (2), printed p.6.
